The workshop, held from November 9 to 11, 2026, at the Corinthia Hotel, brought together NCS management and officers, Trade Modernisation Project Limited (TMPL) and CB-XP representatives to assess the system’s implementation and identify areas requiring technical and operational improvements.
The resolutions reached at the workshop are expected to strengthen trade facilitation, enhance accountability and improve the efficiency of customs operations.
Speaking at the opening ceremony, the Deputy Comptroller-General of Customs in charge of ICT Modernisation, Oluyomi Adebakin, commended the Comptroller-General of Customs, Adewale Adeniyi, for his support for innovation and capacity development within the Service.
The Managing Director of TMPL, Jummai Umar-Ajijola, who represented the Chairman, Saleh Ahmadu, said the B’Odogwu system had attracted interest from the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Secretariat.
She added that improvements to the platform had generated higher revenue and strengthened the revenue ecosystem.
“We are to work to find a concrete plan not only to consolidate but to build a change roadmap going forward at the assessment of the three years so far,” Umar-Ajijola said.
She also commended the NCS Public Relations Unit for its consistent reporting on the project.
Among the major resolutions was the upgrading of the Electronic Cargo Tracking System (ECTS), alongside measures to strengthen bond and transit management, automate customs procedure code approvals and improve the processing of import, export, re-importation and transit declarations.
Participants also agreed on the need to harmonise procedure code nomenclature to promote consistency, efficiency and accountability in customs operations.
On cargo tracking, the workshop reviewed plans to integrate the upgraded ECTS with B’Odogwu and replace 200 obsolete electronic seals with 2,000 newly procured units.
The proposed improvements also include individual container tracking for relevant transit declarations, better bond registration and validation, as well as stronger controls over bonded cargo movements to minimise diversion.
The workshop further examined the integration of B’Odogwu with the Nigeria Export Processing Zones Authority (NEPZA), improvements to the Transire Processing System and upgrades to the platform’s reporting dashboard, search filters and Harmonised System (HS) Code search functionality.
Other proposed improvements include access to previously processed declarations, better monitoring of procedure code applications and system alerts to minimise processing errors.
Participants also agreed on the incorporation of Time Release Study requirements into the platform to improve monitoring of cargo clearance timelines and identify operational bottlenecks.
In addition, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for Bond Management, Transire Commands and Export Commands were reviewed to ensure compliance with the Nigeria Customs Service Act 2023.
To strengthen project governance, participants resolved that all requests for system modifications must be reviewed and approved by the Officer in Charge of the Project Management Office before deployment.
The workshop also reviewed the project’s communication plan to improve stakeholder engagement and ensure better coordination among the NCS, TMPL and other relevant parties.
At the closing ceremony on November 11, the Deputy Comptroller of Customs in charge of Finance, Administration and Technical Services (FATS), Kikelomo Adeola, stressed the need for effective implementation of the resolutions.
The ceremony featured a presentation by the Customs Area Controller, Comptroller Murtala Mu’azu, while the Chairman of CB-XP, Edward Bowen, delivered goodwill remarks.
Specific responsibilities were assigned to relevant NCS and TMPL units to ensure that the resolutions translate into practical improvements in the B’Odogwu system, particularly in cargo clearance, tracking efficiency and revenue collection.
